title: Fearless concurrency: threads, channels, Arc<Mutex>
hints: Look at the README's 'New syntax' table. `parallel_sum` uses `thread::scope` (so the threads can borrow `xs`); the others use `thread::spawn`, so everything a thread uses must be owned: `move` closures, `Arc::clone`s, cloned `Sender`s.

Ideas: `parallel_sum` splits `xs` with `chunks`, spawns one scoped thread per chunk and sums the joined results; `map_threads` puts `f` in an `Arc`, gives each thread a clone of it and of the `Sender`, sends `(index, result)`, then sorts by index; `hammer` spawns threads that lock and increment, keeps their `JoinHandle`s and joins them all; the worker loops `for line in rx` and sends back the length.

'still running after 20s' usually means a receiver is waiting for a sender that never goes away: drop the original `tx` once every worker has its clone. E0373 'closure may outlive the current function' means `thread::spawn` needs a `move` closure; E0277 '`Rc<…>` cannot be sent between threads safely' means use `Arc`.

Same shapes on other data: `thread::scope(|s| { for part in pixels.chunks_mut(64) { s.spawn(move || brighten(part)); } });` · `let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(); for url in urls { let tx = tx.clone(); thread::spawn(move || tx.send(fetch(&url)).unwrap()); } drop(tx);` · `let hits = Arc::new(Mutex::new(0)); let h = Arc::clone(&hits); thread::spawn(move || *h.lock().unwrap() += 1);`
